description: Main command-line interface for managing this device's Tailscale connection.
Show the installed Tailscale client version.
Show devices in the tailnet and their connection status.
Print status as JSON for scripts; JSON fields can change between versions.
Show local status without listing peer details, where supported by the installed version.
Print this device's Tailscale IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, if available.
Print only this device's Tailscale IPv4 address.
Print only this device's Tailscale IPv6 address.
Print one address, preferring IPv4.
Show the Tailscale IP addresses for another device by its tailnet hostname.
Check that this device has the specified Tailscale IP; useful in scripts.
Connect to Tailscale and start authentication if required.
Connect while resetting unspecified preferences to their defaults; review settings first.
Require this device to authenticate again.
Set the device hostname used by Tailscale and potentially MagicDNS.
Do not use DNS settings supplied by the tailnet.
Accept DNS settings supplied by the tailnet.
Accept subnet routes advertised by other devices; availability and defaults vary by OS.
Advertise a local subnet such as 192.168.1.0/24; an administrator may still need to approve it.
Offer this device as an exit node; enable/approve it in the admin console as required.
Route internet traffic through the named exit node; the node must be available and permitted.
Stop using an exit node by explicitly clearing the setting.
Allow access to the client's local LAN while using an exit node.
Block incoming connections from other tailnet devices; outgoing connections can still work.
Enable Tailscale SSH on supported systems, subject to tailnet policy.
Assign approved device tags; the policy must authorize this device to use the tag.
Clear advertised tags by passing an explicitly empty value.
Authenticate using an auth key; avoid exposing the key in shell history or logs.
Read an auth key from a file; protect the file and its permissions.
Use a custom control server, for example a Headscale server, instead of the default.
Limit how long the command waits for the daemon to initialize.
Disconnect this device from the tailnet without uninstalling Tailscale.
Log this device out; authentication will be required again before reconnecting.
Start the login/authentication flow.
Switch to another saved Tailscale account or profile, if profiles are available.
Change only the DNS acceptance preference without restating all `up` options.
Change whether advertised subnet routes are accepted; platform support may vary.
Set the exit node preference without restating every connection option.
Clear the configured exit node.
Block incoming connections from other tailnet devices.
Stop blocking incoming tailnet connections, subject to ACL and firewall rules.
Test reachability to a tailnet device and show whether the path is direct or relayed.
Show additional details while testing reachability.
Stop waiting after the specified duration if the peer cannot be reached.
Do not wait for a direct connection; useful when a relay path is acceptable.
Diagnose network conditions that can affect direct peer-to-peer connections.
Generate a bug-report identifier for troubleshooting; share it with support when requested.
Stream daemon logs for live troubleshooting; it does not retrieve old logs.
Display local preference details for troubleshooting; output may contain sensitive configuration.
Show low-level network-map information for troubleshooting; output can be verbose or sensitive.
Show the tailnet identity associated with a Tailscale IP and optional port.
Return whois information as JSON; put `--json` before the IP argument.
Make a TCP connection test to a peer and port; the service must be listening and allowed.
Open an SSH session using Tailscale SSH where enabled and allowed by policy.
Attempt an SSH connection using the default local username, depending on client and configuration.
Request or manage a TLS certificate for a tailnet hostname; DNS and policy requirements apply.
Write certificate and key to specified files; protect the private key.
Show DNS configuration and status on supported versions.
Open or start the local Tailscale web interface where supported.
Update the Tailscale client where supported; package-manager installs may need the package manager instead.
Skip interactive confirmation for an update where this flag is supported.
Show daemon version information where supported.
Print shell completion code for Bash; follow the output instructions to enable it.
Print shell completion code for Zsh.
Print shell completion code for Fish.
Show services currently shared privately within the tailnet.
Show Serve status as JSON; its schema may differ from the normal status output.
Expose a local HTTP service to devices in the tailnet, typically through HTTPS and MagicDNS.
Expose a local service over HTTPS to the tailnet on the selected port.
Expose a local service over HTTP to the tailnet; use HTTPS when appropriate.
Run Serve in the background so it persists until disabled or reset.
Disable a previously configured Serve target; flags and target may need to match the original configuration.
Remove the current Serve configuration from this device.
Show configuration for all Tailscale Services hosted by this node.
Show services exposed publicly to the internet through Funnel.
Show Funnel status as JSON; the JSON format can change.
Expose a local service publicly through Funnel; anyone on the internet may be able to reach it.
Run Funnel in the background; check status and confirm the service is safe for public access.
Disable a previously configured Funnel target; required flags may need to match the original configuration.
Remove the current Funnel configuration from this device.
Send a file to another tailnet device's Tailscale file inbox.
Receive a file from another device's Tailscale file inbox; check supported syntax on your client version.
Download incoming Tailscale file transfers to a local directory.
Wait for incoming files and download them as they arrive.
Continuously receive files as they arrive, where supported.
Manage Tailscale Drive features where available; feature support and syntax vary by version.
List available exit nodes where supported by the installed version.
Show tailnet lock status where Tailnet Lock is enabled.
Initialize Tailnet Lock where supported; this is a security-sensitive operation.
Authorize a node key with Tailnet Lock; verify the key carefully before approving.
Remove a node key from Tailnet Lock authorization; may affect device connectivity.
Display available Tailscale metrics where supported; output depends on client version.
Show app connector route status where app connectors are configured.
Show learned domains and routes plus extra configured routes.
On systemd Linux, inspect whether the Tailscale daemon service is running.
Start the Tailscale daemon on systemd Linux.
Stop the Tailscale daemon; all Tailscale connectivity on this host will stop.
Restart the Tailscale daemon; active connections may briefly drop.
Enable the daemon at boot and start it now on systemd Linux.
Show available systemd journal logs for the Tailscale daemon.
Follow live Tailscale daemon logs.
Show daemon logs from the last hour.
Open the locally installed manual page if the package provides one.
Show help and supported flags for a command on the installed client version.
Show general CLI help where supported; use `tailscale <command> --help` for command-specific help.
Acknowledge the risk of losing SSH access for operations that may interrupt connectivity; use only when intended.
Disable Tailscale-managed Linux netfilter rules; you must configure firewall rules securely yourself.
Create/manage Tailscale firewall chains without diverting traffic automatically; advanced Linux networking only.
Disable source NAT for advertised subnet routes on Linux; return routing must be configured correctly.
Enable stateful filtering for subnet routers and exit nodes on supported Linux clients.
Publish a local service under a URL path; ensure the backend supports the path setup.
Proxy to a local HTTPS service with an invalid or self-signed certificate; encryption remains but certificate validation is bypassed.
Publish a local service publicly on an allowed Funnel HTTPS port; verify authentication and data exposure first.
Publish a local service publicly using Funnel's allowed HTTPS port 8443.
Publish a local service publicly using Funnel's allowed HTTPS port 10000.
Explicitly reject routes advertised by other devices.
Clear the list of advertised subnet routes by passing an empty value.
Stop offering this device as an exit node.
Disable Tailscale SSH on this device.
On supported Windows clients, keep Tailscale running after the current user logs out.
Get only the IPv4 address for a specified peer where supported by the installed version.
Use a hostname or Tailscale IP; failure can indicate policy, DNS, device state, or network issues.
If unsupported by your client version, run `tailscale status --help` to see accepted flags.
Check exact Serve syntax; Serve/Funnel command syntax changed in Tailscale v1.52.
Check exact Funnel syntax; public exposure can require admin settings and an eligible port.
